icons.name: tripod
icons.heading: Tripod
icons.description: The camera is set down on the tripod and the tripod takes its weight. Light: the stand lifts a little with its legs drawn in, then plants: the hub drops and the feet splay out on the ground as the head lands, and the stand springs back once. Strong: a higher lift, a harder plant with the feet spreading wider, two decaying rebounds, and the camera head rocks forward on its mount as it lands and levels again. The feet never leave the ground line.

icons.name: aperture
icons.heading: Aperture
icons.description: Open to stopped down: the six blades sweep in together and close the iris to a small opening, like an aperture ring clicking to a smaller f-stop. Light: one decisive close that stops dead on the stop, bounces open a little off it and settles. Strong: the iris stops down in two clicks, half way and then fully, each landing with a bounce, the second harder. The ring never moves. Reverse opens the blades again.

icons.heading: Exposure

icons.name: brightness
icons.heading: Brightness
icons.description: Brightness turns up. Light: the lit half of the disc spreads across the dark half until the disc is full, and the light pours out through the rays: each ray shoots out in turn, clockwise from the top, and springs back; then the disc eases back to half. Strong: the brightness steps up in two clicks: the disc fills to three quarters with a first, shorter wave of rays, then to full with a second, longer wave that overshoots and settles, before the disc dims back to half.

icons.name: saturation
icons.heading: Saturation
icons.description: Low to high: colour is added and the saturation rises. Light: a drop of colour forms under the tip, falls through the drop and lands in the colour; on contact the level rises from a fifth to just above half in one decisive fill while the surface sloshes and settles level. Strong: two drops land in turn and the level climbs in two clicks that stop dead, each landing sloshing the surface harder. The level never overshoots and the drop never moves. Reverse drains the colour back down with a small slosh as it lands.
